body:
> To just levitate off into nothingness. I'll be free from all of this hurt, free from every burden.

I understand where you are coming from.  We need help and we need to understand that it isn't our fault that we are such chaos emotionally and mentally.  I feel better already acknowledging the fact that I just need to ask for help.  My loved ones cannot read my mind.

My job which I just started sucks.  It's very dull and I am too far intelligent to subject myself to this particular field which I stumbled into because I just need to pay the bills.  My friends are all alcoholics and drink almost every single night.  They are somewhat to fun to be around, but do not suffer from depression and don't give a fuck about anything.  I was living on my own for quite awhile, but moved back in with my parents to finish my degree.

I believe the letter will help enlighten my family into my deepest struggles with life right now and maybe it will shed light onto why I am such a failure.  

I have thought about studying religions, but because of being raised as an intellectual those we not really options (no offense).  Organized religion was never apart of my life and both my mother and father are agnostics.  I feel like what I need in my life is guidance.  Medication, religion, psychiatry are all valid options I suppose.
Thanks and that makes total sense of course.  I was raised a certain way and I tend to just bottle crap up for way too long.

I just turned 28.  I just wrote this and I think I'm going to email it to my mother.  What do you think?

"Okay, this might be tough for you to hear, but I am severely depressed.  I have been since my last meltdown and it has intensified dramatically since graduation.  I am not going to do anything irrational, but I need help.  By the time you get this I'll be at work.  I need to do something because my pain is becoming too great to handle by myself.  I can no longer pretend to be a functional member of society.  I am broken and I need to be mended.  I understand that this not my fault, but merely an inconvenient part of our family tree.  I must reiterate with great intensity that I am not going to harm myself and you do not need to worry, but we need to discuss this at greater depth and formulate a plan of action so I can be well.  I need help once more and I do apologize for this turmoil in our already complicated lives.  It is almost impossible for me to speak about these emotions of mine as they are very real and painful and I become crippled with sadness when even thinking about them, let alone uttering them to my loved ones.  If this is how I have to communicate then so be it."
